name: Chair Finder (human-reviewed questionnaire, 'Aligna' assistant)
description: Multi-question chair-fit questionnaire fronted by a named virtual assistant persona. Answers are sent to human ergonomic specialists who email back personalized chair recommendations, free and no-obligation. Optional upsell to a paid online assessment with an independent certified ergonomist.
mechanics: Inputs: height (4'10"-6'8"+), weight band (to 701+ lbs), upholstery, headrest, lumbar vs flat back, cushion firmness, sitting posture (upright/forward/reclined), fixed vs adjustable desk, desk height at lowest position, keyboard on desk vs tray, budget band, delivery region, free-text discomfort, opt-in to $100/$150 ergonomist consult, contact. Output: lead form submission -> email recommendations from staff (no instant result).
notes: Lead-gen, not instant. Instant on-page results would beat it; delivery region question surfaces showroom.

name: Monitor Arm Finder
description: Questionnaire for choosing a monitor arm/mount. Specialists review answers and email recommendations.
mechanics: Inputs: mount type (clamp/grommet/bolt-through/wall/pole/ceiling/cart), number+layout of monitors (1-6, rows/stacked), monitor weight band, monitor size, height-adjustment range needed (incl. 20"+ sit-stand), horizontal reach, design tier (best-in-class/value/minimum cost), sit vs sit-stand, delivery region, user height, contact. Output: emailed recommendations.
notes: Lacks an automatic VESA/weight compatibility check; Jestik could output matching arms instantly.

name: Standing Desk Finder
description: Questionnaire for full height-adjustable desks with explanations of each lift mechanism and surface shape/size picker.
mechanics: Inputs: user height, mechanism (electric/pneumatic/crank/pin-set, each explained), surface shape (rectangular, equal corner 2/3-leg, offset L 2/3-leg), surface size list, left/right orientation, budget, delivery, contact. Output: emailed recommendations. Includes an ergonomic evaluation widget below.

name: Desk Finder (standing desk vs converter chooser)
description: Gateway page that asks whether you want a full standing desk or a desk converter, with a side-by-side comparison table to help decide, and links to all other finders.
mechanics: Input: one choice (standing desk / converter). Output: routes to the specific finder. Static comparison table rows: what it is, what moves, best for, worth knowing.
notes: Good decision-support pattern ('X vs Y' table).

name: Desk Converter Finder
description: Questionnaire for sit-stand desktop converters based on existing desk dimensions and equipment; includes long FAQ section on converters.
mechanics: Inputs: desk height, depth, width (dropdowns), user height, monitor/laptop setup, budget band, delivery region, monitor make/model, special requirements, contact. Output: emailed recommendations. Page carries SEO FAQ (converter vs desk etc.).

name: Mobile Cart Finder
description: Questionnaire for rolling computer carts (healthcare WOW, POS, education, warehouse) with FAQ on powered vs non-powered carts.
mechanics: Inputs: user height, number/type of displays, budget, delivery region, device model, special requirements. Output: emailed recommendations.
notes: Niche for a home/office store; B2B healthcare focus.

name: All Product Finders hub
description: Landing page listing the finders and explaining that real humans (not algorithms) review answers.
mechanics: Static cards linking to each finder with a one-line purpose; value proposition bullets (personalized, human-reviewed, practical).
notes: Outdated: says 'our four product finders' while 6 finders exist (desk-converter and desk-finder missing from list).

name: Workspace Planner / Ergonomic Desk Height Calculator
description: Click-your-height calculator based on BIFMA G1 anthropometric data that shows recommended monitor, keyboard and seat heights for sitting and standing, plus sit-stand travel needed. Suggests matching sit-stand products and offers a printable worksheet.
mechanics: Input: user height via buttons 5'0"-6'4" (1" steps). Output: 7 values (e.g., for 5'8": standing/sitting monitor height, standing/sitting keyboard height, seat height 18", sit-stand adjustment 18"), a diagram with 20-30" viewing distance and 10-20 deg tilt, 'install within an inch' instruction, product suggestions by height, printable worksheet.
notes: Height range only 5'0"-6'4" (excludes petite/tall users who need it most); no metric; heights hard-coded in data attributes. Easy to beat with a slider, cm/in toggle, shoe allowance, and links to products whose ranges fit.

name: Ergonomic Evaluation Tool (7-question self-assessment, sitewide)
description: Seven yes/no checklist questions about the user's current workstation, shown on most resource pages. Each 'No' highlights a body area on a figure and shows a corrective tip; results can be sent to ErgoDirect specialists.
mechanics: Inputs: yes/no for monitor top at eye level, >=20" viewing distance, flat wrists, relaxed shoulders, feet flat with 90-120 deg hips, adjustability of monitor/keyboard/chair, standing periodically. Output: per-question fix text (e.g., bifocal monitor guidance), body-diagram highlights (neck/eye/wrist/shoulder/low back), 'See Recommendations', 'Send Results' to staff (lead capture).
notes: Simple but effective; Jestik could add scoring, product links per failed item and a downloadable PDF report.

name: Ergotron Mount Finder (embedded)
description: Page meant to embed Ergotron's partner mount finder in an iframe.
mechanics: iframe to ergotron.com/en-us/partner-finder/ergodirect.
notes: Appears broken: the embedded Ergotron URL returned HTTP 403 when fetched; page has no other content. Fixed 800px iframe not mobile friendly.

name: 3D Chair Configurator ('Build your ... chair in 3D')
description: Selected Office Master/OM Seating chairs have a 3D build experience where option choices (upholstery, arms, cylinder, etc.) update a rendered chair; product cards are labeled 'Build your X chair in 3D'. Product page also embeds the manufacturer's interactive adjustment demo.
mechanics: Inputs: option swatches/selectors per chair. Output: updated 3D/visual preview with progress bar loader, running price, add to cart. Separate iframe from omseating.com shows chair adjustment animations.
notes: Heavy (1MB+ page). Valuable for configurable chairs; costly to build unless supplier provides assets.

name: Product option/add-on configurator with 'My Selections' summary
description: Product pages list required model choice plus optional add-ons (CPU holder, notebook tray, cables, mats, mouse holder) each with 'No thanks', and a summary panel of selections.
mechanics: Inputs: per-option click-to-select with quantity variants. Output: 'All Options / My Selections' summary, price update, add to cart.
notes: Good model for accessory attach (bundles/add-ons). Some options outdated (VGA/DVI cables).

name: Seat Height Measurement Guide
description: Explains popliteal height, gas cylinder sizes (4/5/6 inch) and how seat-height range relates to cylinder choice, with step-by-step home measuring instructions.
mechanics: Static guide + infographic: sit with feet flat, measure floor to just below kneecap; aim for measurement mid-range of the chair's adjustment; suggests footrest if desk forces raised seat.
notes: Ideal to convert into an interactive cylinder/seat-height checker.

name: Seat Width & Depth Measurement Guide
description: How to measure seat width (books against hips) and seat depth (buttock-to-knee minus ~2") to pick a chair that fits.
mechanics: Static steps + infographic; explains consequences of too narrow/wide/deep/shallow.

name: Elbow Height Measurement (armrest)
description: Short image-led guide to measuring elbow height for setting chair armrests.
mechanics: One sentence + image instructions; recommends a helper.
notes: Thin content (image only, ~2 sentences).

name: ErgoTips
description: Bullet-point setup tips by component: chair, monitor, keyboard, mouse, desk; each section links to the matching finder or planner.
mechanics: Static tips (e.g., arm's-length monitor distance, curved monitor viewing distance from curvature radius, negative keyboard tilt, standard desk height 28-30", alternate sit/stand every 20-30 min).
notes: Cross-links tips to tools - good internal linking pattern.

name: Installation videos / Cylinder replacement video
description: Pages embedding a single YouTube video each (chair gas cylinder replacement; general installation).
mechanics: YouTube iframe, no transcript or steps.
notes: Very thin pages (title + video). Also /pages/installations.html.

name: Installation case studies
description: Before/after customer stories (3-monitor sit-stand conversion; L-shaped desk keyboard tray with corner diagonal) describing the problem, chosen products and result.
mechanics: Static 'The Need / Solution' narrative with photos and product names.
notes: Only two, old. Also /pages/installation-ergonomic-keyboard-tray-l-shaped-desk.html.

name: FAQ / Answered Questions hub (351 Q&As)
description: Large FAQ page grouped into Choosing products, Creating a better workspace, Getting help, 'Where It Hurts?' (neck, shoulders, low back, legs, wrists), Ordering/Shipping/Support, plus aggregated product Q&A by product/brand.
mechanics: Static accordion; answers cross-link to finders, planner and measurement guides. Pain-based section maps symptoms to adjustments.
notes: Page is ~1.1MB HTML; 'Where It Hurts' symptom navigation is the standout idea.

name: Blog (Ergonomics 101 & Office Resources)
description: WordPress blog with ~112 posts: chair choice for petite users, desk too high, sit-stand lowest height, VESA explainer, cylinder choice, keyboard trays, gaming ergonomics, WFH, comparison charts.
mechanics: Post list with categories: Ergonomics, Monitor Arm, Work From Home, Thermal Imaging Cart.
notes: Many posts 2018-2020 era; 'thermal imaging cart' category and COVID WFH posts are dated. Strong evergreen petite-user angle.

name: Office Master arms comparison chart
description: Matrix of armrest models vs chair series showing compatibility.
mechanics: Static table: arm model, type, description, X marks per chair series.
notes: Pattern useful as accessory compatibility matrix.

name: Product downloads tab (spec sheets, drawings, installation PDFs)
description: Product pages include a Downloads tab with manufacturer product sheets, technical drawings and installation guides, plus a Technical Drawing and Specifications tab.
mechanics: Linked PDFs under /attachments/doc/... per component.

name: Product Q&A ('Ask a Question') per product
description: FAQ tab on each product where shoppers can ask a question; answered questions are aggregated into the sitewide FAQ.
mechanics: Input: question form. Output: staff-answered Q&A shown on product and in /resources/answered-questions.
notes: Many products show 'No FAQs available'.

name: Product reviews with star histogram + Google Customer Reviews
description: Native product reviews with 5-to-1 star breakdown and 'Write a review'; site loads Google Customer Reviews script for post-purchase surveys/badge.
mechanics: Review form (submit-review), rating histogram; Google platform.js renderGoogleCustomerReviews.
notes: Most products have very few reviews (e.g., 1).

name: Store-level Customer Reviews page
description: Paginated list of 181 store reviews, many praising named sales reps (chat, tax-exempt help, showroom visit).
mechanics: Static paginated list, 25 per page; testimonials also rotate on homepage.

name: Live chat (SnapEngage)
description: Live chat widget staffed by sales reps; reviews cite chat help with options and orders.
mechanics: SnapEngage JS widget, proactive chat disabled.

name: Wishlist (account-gated)
description: Save-for-later list tied to customer account; heart icons on product cards.
mechanics: Redirects to login when not signed in.
notes: Requires login; guest wishlist would be friendlier.

name: Corporate discounts / quote requests
description: Robots.txt references corp_discounts.php, /quote/ and /instant_quote/ endpoints, indicating corporate discount and quote workflows; homepage pitches corporate solutions and free consultations.
mechanics: Not crawled (disallowed in robots.txt). Homepage: 'Free Consultation', 'Custom Products', corporate office solution tiles.
notes: Mechanics not verified (disallowed paths respected).

name: Ergo-Stream (corporate ergonomics program for EHS/HR)
description: B2B program bundling online workstation evaluations, customized assessment questionnaires, private pre-approved catalog with negotiated prices, account executive, ergonomic lab setup, and per-employee inventory/financial reporting.
mechanics: Static description + lead form (requirements free text, name, email, company, phone).
notes: Strong model for a Jestik 'Teams/Business' program.

name: Office Layout & Design services

mechanics: Static text sections.
notes: Contains garbled copy ('an error direct fuses our deep expertise') - looks unedited/outdated.

mechanics: Badge + shipping note near price.

name: Free consultation / ergonomist assessment upsell

mechanics: Static text.
notes: Customer-unfriendly; a simple Jestik policy (e.g., free returns / 30-day trial on stock items) would differentiate.

description: Detailed service page: on-site and virtual workstation evaluations, workshops, workstation design, chair fittings, with what's included, process steps, industries, cities served, and FAQ.
